summary: Local neighborhood groups, schools-oriented clubs and corporate sponsors launched a series of tree planting drives across town in September 2023. Events ranged from AENA's 200-resident planting to a free sapling giveaway, a family educational day, and Atlas Electronics' tree-matching program. Experts guided species choices, and organizers worked around urban obstacles using raised planters and smaller species.
one_line: Town neighborhood associations, clubs and Atlas Electronics ran September 2023 tree planting drives to boost urban greenery, education and climate resilience.
key_facts: The Arbor Enthusiast Neighborhood Association (AENA) mobilized over 200 residents for a tree planting effort on September 5, 2023.
Susan Martinez has led AENA for the past three years and said trees 'clean our air, provide shade, and become a habitat for wildlife.'
AENA partnered with the local horticultural society to identify suitable native species for the urban setting.
Dr. Emily Rios, an ecologist at the city's Environmental Planning Office, advised neighborhood associations on species suited to soil, climate and urban planning needs.
Oaks, maples and native flowering species were chosen for their resilience and ecological benefits.
Dr. Rios said tree planting helps mitigate urban heat islands, reduce stormwater runoff and enhance biodiversity.
The Green Thumb Circle held an event on September 12, 2023 with the slogan 'Your Yard, Your Tree, Our Future,' distributing free saplings at local parks.
Mia Zhang is president of the Green Thumb Circle and said the approach makes environmental action 'very personal and immediate.'

On September 18, 2023, the Young Explorers Club and the Botanical Academy hosted a family-friendly planting day with talks on photosynthesis, the carbon cycle and local ecosystem balance, led by Tom Nguyen.
On September 25, 2023, Atlas Electronics sponsored a city-wide initiative matching each tree planted by a citizen with one planted by the company.
Atlas CEO Jennifer O'Donnell said the goal is to 'double the impact of individual efforts'; the initiative led to thousands of trees planted and inspired other businesses.
Urban obstacles include underground utilities, pedestrian traffic and restricted planting zones; solutions include raised planters and smaller species.
The Riverside Residents Association (RRA) turned concrete-bound street corners into green pockets on the weekend of September 30.
